get.description: ## Search Terms Features Most PowerQuery fields support a number of search terms features. Support is indicated in the field description. ### Boolean Operators Boolean operators are used to create various combinations of search terms to be used in supported fields. By default, all terms are optional, as long as one term matches. A search for foo bar baz will find any document that contains one or more of foo or bar or baz. Possible operators are: OR (Default) For example, a query string of capital of Hungary is interpreted as capital OR of OR Hungary and would return results containing any of these 3 terms. AND For example, a query string of capital AND Hungary would only return results that contain both terms captial *AND* Hungary. NOT For example, a query string of capital AND NOT Hungary would only return results that contain the term captial *AND does NOT* contain the term Hungary. ### Grouping Multiple terms or clauses can be grouped together with parentheses, to form sub-queries: ``` (quick OR brown) AND fox ``` **NOTE:** Parentheses should be always whenever multiple operators are used together. For example: ``` ((quick AND fox) OR (brown AND fox) OR fox) AND NOT news ``` ### Exact phrases Since separating the terms with spaces is treated as the `OR` operator it is possible to wrap multiple terms in double quotes to search for exact occurence of the phrase. For example: ``` "capital of Hungary" ``` will return results containing the exact phrase with no values in between the three terms. ### Wildcards Wildcard searches can be run on individual terms, using `?` to replace a single character, and `*` to replace zero or more characters: ``` qu?ck bro* ``` ### Ranges Ranges can be specified for most numeric fields. Inclusive ranges are specified with square brackets `[min TO max]` and exclusive ranges with curly brackets `{min TO max}`. - Numbers 1..5 ``` company_total_shipments=[1 TO 5] ``` - Numbers greater than 10 ``` company_total_shipments=[10 TO *] ``` - Numbers less than 500 ``` supplier_total_shipments=[* TO 500] ``` **Data credits:** 1 per 10 records returned, scaled to how many records are in this response. The `requestCost` field on success is the data credits charged for the call.

get.description: ## Search Terms Features Most PowerQuery fields support a number of search terms features. Support is indicated in the field description. ### Boolean Operators Boolean operators are used to create various combinations of search terms to be used in supported fields. By default, all terms are optional, as long as one term matches. A search for foo bar baz will find any document that contains one or more of foo or bar or baz. Possible operators are: OR (Default) For example, a query string of capital of Hungary is interpreted as capital OR of OR Hungary and would return results containing any of these 3 terms. AND For example, a query string of capital AND Hungary would only return results that contain both terms captial *AND* Hungary. NOT For example, a query string of capital AND NOT Hungary would only return results that contain the term captial *AND does NOT* contain the term Hungary. ### Grouping Multiple terms or clauses can be grouped together with parentheses, to form sub-queries: ``` (quick OR brown) AND fox ``` **NOTE:** Parentheses should be always whenever multiple operators are used together. For example: ``` ((quick AND fox) OR (brown AND fox) OR fox) AND NOT news ``` ### Exact phrases Since separating the terms with spaces is treated as the `OR` operator it is possible to wrap multiple terms in double quotes to search for exact occurence of the phrase. For example: ``` "capital of Hungary" ``` will return results containing the exact phrase with no values in between the three terms. ### Wildcards Wildcard searches can be run on individual terms, using `?` to replace a single character, and `*` to replace zero or more characters: ``` qu?ck bro* ``` ### Ranges Ranges can be specified for most numeric fields. Inclusive ranges are specified with square brackets `[min TO max]` and exclusive ranges with curly brackets `{min TO max}`. - Numbers 1..5 ``` company_total_shipments=[1 TO 5] ``` - Numbers greater than 10 ``` company_total_shipments=[10 TO *] ``` - Numbers less than 500 ``` supplier_total_shipments=[* TO 500] ``` **Data credits:** 1 per 10 records returned, scaled to how many records are in this response. The `requestCost` field on success is the data credits charged for the call.

info.title: ImportYeti Data API Documentation
info.description: This **beta** API implementation allows searching and fetching ImportYeti data. **Data credits** are the credits you purchase and see in your balance. Each documented endpoint states its **data credit** cost. Where a route charges data credits, successful responses include `requestCost` (credits consumed for that call) and `creditsRemaining` (balance after the call). **TOON responses:** add `?format=toon` to any endpoint to get the same data as [TOON](https://github.com/toon-format/toon) instead of JSON — a compact text encoding that costs fewer tokens when the response is fed to an LLM. It is entirely optional; without the parameter every response stays JSON, and errors are always JSON. For guides, code samples, and the full endpoint reference, see the documentation at [docs.importyeti.com](https://docs.importyeti.com). Buy More Credits
